Prepare a corpus once for several topic models

Source: R/topics.R
topic_corpus.Rd

topic_corpus() prepares a corpus once for several topic models: it segments the texts, embeds them, and tokenizes them for term scoring, and returns a prepared corpus that topics() and compare_topics() accept in place of the texts. Fitting topic models usually means fitting several (different numbers of topics, term settings, or seeds on the same texts), and these three steps do not depend on any of those choices; embedding is by far the most expensive step.

Models fitted to the corpus are identical to models fitted to the raw texts. The corpus fixes the embeddings (from model or embeddings), the segmentation, and the tokenization settings; the settings of each model, such as n_topics, n_terms, weighting, and seeds, are still chosen per call. The result is an object of class sbert_topic_corpus.

compare_topics() builds a corpus itself, so a corpus is needed only when models are fitted one at a time.

Usage

topic_corpus(
  text,
  column = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  embeddings = NULL,
  batch_size = 32L,
  stop_words = default_stop_words(),
  min_token_length = 2L,
  stem = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  numbers = c("keep", "remove"),
  roman_numerals = c("keep", "remove"),
  section_numbers = c("keep", "remove"),
  segment = c("document", "sentence", "clause", "phrase"),
  max_tokens = NULL,
  merge_below = 0L,
  min_content = 0
)

Arguments

text

Documents: a character vector with one document per element, or a data frame together with column.

column

Name of the text column when text is a data frame. The other columns are carried into the document table. Rows whose text is missing, blank, or the placeholder "[No abstract available]" are dropped, and so are their rows of embeddings. NULL (default) for a character vector.

model

The encoder: a model from load_model(), a pinned model name from models(), or NULL (default) for the default model. Not used when embeddings are given.

embeddings

Optional numeric matrix of precomputed embeddings, one row per modeled unit (per document, or per segment with segment). When it is given, no model is loaded. Default NULL.

batch_size

Texts encoded per model call (default 32).

stop_words

Words excluded from the topic terms; default stop_words(). character() turns the filter off.

min_token_length

Minimum length of a term, in characters (default 2).

stem

Whether to merge inflected forms of a term under one Porter stem, shown as its most frequent form (default FALSE; needs the SnowballC package).

cores

Number of forked worker processes for tokenization (default 1; Unix-alikes only). Results do not depend on it.

numbers, roman_numerals, section_numbers

Whether to "keep" (default) or "remove" digit-only tokens, Roman-numeral tokens, and section or list numbering (1.2.3, 1.) from the topic terms. They change the terms only, not the text that is embedded; to clean the text, use clean_corpus().

segment

Unit of analysis: "document" (default), or "sentence", "clause", or "phrase", which split each document with segment() and fit the topics to the segments, so that a document can take part in several topics.

max_tokens, merge_below, min_content

Segmentation options passed to segment(), for segmented fits only: the maximum segment length (in the model's tokens, or in words with precomputed embeddings; default NULL, no limit), the number of words below which a segment is joined to its neighbor (default 0), and the minimum share of letters for a segment to be kept (default 0; see content_ratio()).

Value

An object of class sbert_topic_corpus. Its units (one row per document, or per segment) are given by as.data.frame(); printing it shows the number of documents and segments, the embedding dimension, the model, and the tokenization settings.

Conditions

Errors of class sbert_bad_input when both model and embeddings are given, a document is blank, the embeddings do not have one row per unit, the segmentation produces fewer than two segments, or segment is passed together with an existing corpus; sbert_missing_package for stem = TRUE without SnowballC. When a model is used, the errors of load_model() and encode() apply.

See also

topics() and compare_topics(), which take the corpus; as.data.frame() for its units; segment() for the segmentation.

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
prepared <- topic_corpus(corpus, column = "translation",
                         embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
prepared
#> <sbert_topic_corpus>
#>   documents: 600 
#>   embedding dimension: 384 
#>   model: precomputed embeddings 
#>   tokenization: min_token_length = 2  
topic_sizes(topics(prepared, n_topics = 4))
#>   topic                                                     label n_documents
#> 1     1 Where is the cow and the cake? Choose all the pictures...         405
#> 2     2       What does “all the ones between the leaf and the...         143
#> 3     3  It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting.          27
#> 4     4                     What does it mean to be on the grass?          25
#>   proportion
#> 1 0.67500000
#> 2 0.23833333
#> 3 0.04500000
#> 4 0.04166667
topic_sizes(topics(prepared, n_topics = 6))
#>   topic                                                       label n_documents
#> 1     1   Where is the cow and the cake? Choose all the pictures...         223
#> 2     2            All the ones between the cat and the strawberry.         133
#> 3     3         What does “all the ones between the leaf and the...         131
#> 4     4 Are you sure you have fewer pictures in the red box than...          49
#> 5     5      In the top middle box, it means something is in the...          37
#> 6     6    It is not a person, does not have a hat, and is sitting.          27
#>   proportion
#> 1 0.37166667
#> 2 0.22166667
#> 3 0.21833333
#> 4 0.08166667
#> 5 0.06166667
#> 6 0.04500000
